what: the clinician sitting: one physician author, 70 items in one sitting; blinding varies by stage

sitting.conflict: the rater is an author of the study and designed the instruments he is grading; sections A, B, C and G are endorsements rather than blind measurements

rows.detail: 10 notes where the two designs reach opposite conclusions, one per consultation; he was told neither which judge said what nor whether the note had been edited

conservative.why: the grid's note-level flag on an errored note can be earned by a defect the item never shows (F4 is a `change` pair, F5 a partial-strong omission of a different fact), so the grid is not adjudicable on the fact the item asks about

rows.detail: one blinded or endorsing pass per pipeline stage

stages.stage: inference-time fact extraction: the cited quote supports the fact
reference-note repair: the flag was a real defect, properly fixed
omission-pair rejection: the panel was right to reject
taxonomy panel cuts: false-kill rate (2 abstentions)

rows.detail: 20 facts graded blind against the written rubric, against the two-arm machine consensus

result.instrument_note: this validates the FACTORIAL severity axis (master/factorial_severity.json, the paper) - the axis results are conditioned on. It does NOT validate the pipeline audit stage's own severity grades, which are what the paper's per-fact decision rule fires on; that is a separate run of the same written rubric and no item in this sitting scores it.
